take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only when access, dialect or stance differ, and ask whether one prompt would do the same.
Handoffs are where errors enter, such as two numbers and one kept. Nothing in this module checks that the final briefing is true.
Before connecting an agent to finance systems, ask what the worst thing is it could do with that access.

monday.move: Ask IT what data and access an agent would get if the controller tried it on month-end variance commentary, and what one run costs.
monday.who: my controller and the IT lead
monday.stop_condition: IT says no approved tool for finance data, or no cost per run can be stated.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and I still have no cost figure.

misconception.why: The module never gave a cost, a payback or an organisational capability to build. It was about technique. The 'one agent unless' slides and the access warning made me more careful, but I still see this as a tool you license and govern.

one_line: Good that it says one agent is the default and names the risks, but I got no figure, no cost per month and no way to check the output, so I have nothing to take to the board.
